text: The 2006 UEFA Champions League final was an association football match between Barcelona of Spain and Arsenal of England, held at the Stade de France in Saint-Denis, Paris, France, on Wednesday, 17 May 2006. It was the final match of the 2005–06 season of the UEFA Champions League, Europe's primary cup competition. Barcelona, appearing in their fifth final and having won the competition once in 1992, reached the final by winning their group stage matches against Chelsea, Benfica, and Milan. Arsenal, making their first (and only) final appearance and becoming the first club from London to do so, won their group without conceding a goal, defeating Real Madrid, Juventus, and Villarreal. Each club played 12 matches in total to reach the final. A crowd of 79,500 watched as Jens Lehmann was sent off early in the game. Despite this, Arsenal took the lead through Sol Campbell in the second half. Henrik Larsson came on for Barcelona after an hour and was involved in both of their goals. Barcelona equalised through Samuel Eto'o near the end of the second half, and Juliano Belletti scored shortly after to give Barcelona a 2–1 victory. This marked the first time Arsenal had appeared in a European Cup final, and they had last reached a European final six years earlier in 2000, when they lost on penalties after a goalless draw against Galatasaray. Of the players from that final, only Thierry Henry and Dennis Bergkamp remained at Arsenal, while Sylvinho, who played in the 2000 final, was now with Barcelona. Barcelona's last final appearance was a 4–0 loss to Milan in 1994, with two prior losses in 1961 and 1986, and their only success in the competition was in 1992 against Sampdoria. Barcelona entered the final as domestic league champions, having won La Liga a fortnight earlier. They were considered the best side in Europe due to players like Ronaldinho and Samuel Eto'o, though Deco dismissed the idea of them being favourites, emphasizing the need for seriousness and concentration. Neither team had been defeated en route to the final; Arsenal conceded only two goals in their 12 matches, including ten consecutive matches without conceding, setting a record of 919 minutes without a goal, while Barcelona had scored 114 goals in all competitions before the final. Arsenal would earn €37.3 million if they won and €34.7 million if they lost, while Barcelona would receive €31.5 million if they won and €28.9 million if they lost. The winners would receive €6.4 million and the runners-up €3.8 million. The final marked the introduction of a new trophy after Liverpool's fifth title, which entitled them to keep the previous one. UEFA selected the Stade de France to host the final after evaluating capacity, infrastructure, and promotional plans, and it had previously hosted the 2000 final between Real Madrid and Valencia. The choice recognized the 50th anniversary of the first European Cup final in 1956, held at the Parc des Princes, now home to Paris Saint-Germain, which also hosted the 1975 and 1981 European Cup finals, the 1978 and 1995 UEFA Cup Winners' Cup finals, and the 1998 UEFA Cup final. Both teams qualified through the group stage: Arsenal by finishing second in the 2004–05 FA Premier League, and Barcelona by winning La Liga. The group stage consisted of eight double round-robin groups of four teams, with the top two advancing to the knockout stage, decided by home and away results, away goals, extra time, and penalties if needed. Barcelona broadcast the match live from their Mini Estadi on a 70-metre television screen, reaching an estimated audience of 15,276. Before the final, an estimated 1.2 million people gathered in Barcelona as the team toured the city on open-top buses to celebrate winning La Liga. On the morning of the final, assistant referee Ole Hermann Borgan was found posing in a Barcelona shirt for a Norwegian newspaper, leading UEFA to replace him with Arild Sundet, as Norway's head of refereeing Rune Pedersen stated that referees must not act in a way that questions their impartiality. Barcelona were expected to play in a 4–2–3–1 formation with Ronaldinho, Ludovic Giuly, and Deco supporting Samuel Eto'o as the lone striker, though doubts existed about Lionel Messi’s fitness after a thigh muscle pull during the Chelsea match; he was included in the 22-man squad but did not play. Barcelona coach Frank Rijkaard stated he would decide on Messi's inclusion late. Arsenal were expected to use a 4–5–1 formation with Thierry Henry as the sole striker, with debate over whether José Antonio Reyes would replace Robert Pires on the left midfield, as Pires had agreed to join Villarreal. Ultimately, Barcelona fielded a 4–3–3 formation with Mark van Bommel and Edmílson in midfield alongside Deco, ahead of Xavi and Andrés Iniesta, while Lionel Messi did not feature in the matchday squad. Arsenal used a 4–4–1–1 formation, with Emmanuel Eboué replacing the injured Lauren and Ashley Cole returning at left-back for only his third appearance in the competition that season. Thierry Henry was the lone striker, with Freddie Ljungberg playing off his shoulder. Both teams wore red kits, so Arsenal wore their yellow away strip and Barcelona their traditional blue and maroon striped kit. Arsenal won the coin toss and Barcelona kicked off. Barcelona faced immediate pressure when Thierry Henry shot straight at goalkeeper Víctor Valdés, who conceded a corner. Henry then had another chance, but Valdés saved the shot. In the seventh minute, Lehmann saved from Ludovic Giuly. Four minutes later, Barcelona were awarded a free-kick 35 yards from goal, which Ronaldinho shot wide. With 18 minutes played, Lehmann was sent off for bringing down Samuel Eto'o outside the Arsenal box, becoming the first player to be sent off in a European Cup final. Giuly then put the ball in the net, but the goal was disallowed due to the foul. Arsenal substituted Robert Pires for Manuel Almunia. The free-kick was sent wide by Ronaldinho. After Lehmann's dismissal, Barcelona increased pressure, leading to a caution for Emmanuel Eboué for a high tackle. In the 37th minute, Arsenal scored when Sol Campbell headed in from a Thierry Henry free-kick after Carles Puyol fouled Eboué. Some believed Eboué had dived. Arsenal held the lead until halftime. Barcelona's best chance came from Eto'o, whose shot hit the post after being saved by Almunia. At half-time, Barcelona replaced Edmílson, who had picked up an injury, with Andrés Iniesta. Almunia saved a shot from Iniesta six minutes into the half. After 61 minutes, Barcelona substituted Van Bommel for Larsson. Minutes later, Alexander Hleb received a pass from Henry but shot wide. Arsenal pressed forward, with Henry and Ljungberg seeing shots saved; Henry then had another chance after being played through by Hleb, but he shot straight at Valdés. Oleguer was replaced by Juliano Belletti, and Arsenal substituted Cesc Fàbregas with Mathieu Flamini. Iniesta sent a pass to Larsson, who one-touch laid it off to Eto'o, who equalised. Four minutes later, Larsson played a one-two with Belletti, and the Brazilian full-back shot through Almunia's legs to score at the near post. In the final minutes, Arsenal replaced Hleb with Reyes in an attempt to equalise, but Barcelona had the best chance, only for Giuly to hit his shot straight at Almunia. Larsson then impeded the goalkeeper and was cautioned. The match ended with Barcelona winning 2–1. With this loss, Arsenal became the first English club and third overall—after Hamburger SV and Fiorentina—to be runners-up in all three major European competitions (UEFA Champions League, UEFA Cup, and Cup Winners' Cup). Samuel Eto'o was named Man of the Match. The assistant referees were Steinar Holvik and Arild Sundet, with Tom Henning Øvrebø as the fourth official. Barcelona captain Carles Puyol collected the trophy from UEFA president Lennart Johansson after their second European Cup victory. Much of the post-match discussion focused on referee Terje Hauge sending off Lehmann. Mark Lawrenson stated, "The game changed when Arsenal goalkeeper Jens Lehmann was sent off," and Arsène Wenger agreed, saying the loss of a player left them with 70 minutes to play with ten against eleven against a team that retained the ball well. Wenger did not openly criticise the decision, though he disputed the offside call on Eto'o's first goal and insisted his young side would recover. Thierry Henry criticised the referee, stating, "I was kicked all over the place. I expected the referee to do his job. I don't think he did." There was speculation about Henry moving to Barcelona, but on 19 May, he signed a four-year contract with Arsenal, ending the rumors. Henrik Larsson, who provided two assists, was delighted and stated he had no regrets about leaving Barcelona, saying he wanted to play more football and felt he hadn't played enough due to the strong competition. Giovanni van Bronckhorst, a Barcelona player, was emotional, saying it was special to win against his former club. Eto'o cited Liverpool's comeback against Milan as inspiration, saying, "After having seen what Liverpool did last year, we told ourselves not to throw in the towel. We followed Liverpool's example." Barcelona manager Frank Rijkaard praised goalkeeper Víctor Valdés, stating he made crucial saves. Thierry Henry paid tribute to Larsson, saying, "People always talk about Ronaldinho, Eto'o, Giuly and everything, but I didn't see them today, I saw Henrik Larsson. He came on, he changed the game, that is what killed the game. Sometimes you talk about Ronaldinho and Eto'o and people like that; you need to talk about the proper footballer who made the difference, and that was Henrik Larsson tonight." He added, "You have to remember that Barcelona is a team. It's not Eto'o, it's not Ronaldinho. On Wednesday, the man who made the difference was Henrik Larsson. You have to give him credit for that because when he came on he made some amazing runs around the box and he showed he is a team player. You saw two times he fed the ball back to people and that's what I always talk about, he is a team player. He did that against us, even though the first goal was a close offside decision." Larsson's introduction was noted by international press as giving Barcelona the edge to overcome Arsenal. As a result of winning the Champions League, Barcelona faced Sevilla, the UEFA Cup winners, in the UEFA Super Cup on 25 August 2006, which Sevilla won 3–0. Barcelona also participated in the FIFA Club World Cup, receiving a bye in the first round, beating Club América 4–0 in the semi-finals, and then facing Copa Libertadores champions Internacional of Brazil, who won 1–0 in the final.
